That is false for over-price-cap, one of the five refusals it enumerates, and one of the four named vectors falsifies it directly: the Meridian fare is median x 2.5 x units x hops, and the median is other players' tariffs. Measured on the real file - a 5,000-unit 5-hop haul quotes ok at 2,500,000 with the board at the floor (median 40) and is REFUSED over-price-cap the moment rivals push the median to 100. sql/038 documents this exact case in the header above transport_quote and reaches the opposite conclusion in writing: Meridian is 'NOT unconditionally answerable, and the difference matters enough to write down... When the market's own median sits at the tariff ceiling, a haul at max_units x max_hops prices above max_price_per_contract and Meridian refuses it too. Measured: 37,500,000 against a cap of 5,000,000.' A file whose entire method is fidelity to that authority inverted it on the one paragraph that states the feature's safety guarantee. The remedy is small and does not weaken the guarantee: say that over-price-cap CAN move with the board, that the remedy is still the shipper's own edit (split the manifest), and that no rival can therefore end anyone's game - which is the true and still-sufficient claim.
